==English== ===Pronunciation=== * {{a|en|horse-hoarse}} ** {{enPR|kôs|a=RP}}, {{IPA|en|/kɔːs/}} ** {{enPR|kôrs|a=GA}}, {{IPA|en|/kɔɹs/}}, {{IPAchar|/koɹs/}}{{R:MWO}} (uses the notation ˈkȯrs, [https://www.merriam-webster.com/assets/mw/static/pdf/help/guide-to-pronunciation.pdf or in IPA] [ˈkoɚs, ˈkɔɚs]){{R:Dictionary.com}} (uses the notation /kɔrs, koʊrs/) *** {{audio|en|en-us-course.ogg|a=GA}} ** {{homophones|en|coarse}} ** {{rhymes|en|ɔː(ɹ)s|s1=1}} * {{a|en|non-horse-hoarse}} ** {{enPR|kōrs|a=rhotic}}, {{IPA|en|/koːɹs/}} ** {{IPA|en|/koəs/|a=non-rhotic}} * {{IPA|en|/kɜːs/|a=Tasmania}} *: {{homophones|en|curse}} {{qualifier|Tasmania}} *: {{rhymes|en|ɜː(ɹ)s|s1=1}} {{qualifier|Tasmania}} * {{q|{{lg|obsolete}}}} {{IPA|en|/kuːɹs/|/kʊɹs/}}{{R:Jespersen MEGoHP|I|13.36|368}} ===Etymology 1=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱers-}} {{etymon|en|id=sequence|:inh|enm:cours|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|cours}}, from {{der|en|fro|cours}}, from {{der|en|la|cursus||course of a race}}, from {{m|la|currō||run}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ḱers-||to run}}. {{doublet|en|cursus|cour}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # A [[sequence]] of [[event]]s. #: {{ux|en|The normal '''course''' of events seems to be just one damned thing after another.}} #* {{RQ:Bramah Bravo of London|passage=Tilehurst would in the ordinary '''course''' have caught him up and they would have progressed companionably wheel by wheel for as far as their way lay together, discussing the simpler aspects of Tapsfield existence.}} ## A normal or customary sequence. ##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Midsummer|act=I|scene=i|passage=The '''course''' of true love never did run smooth.}} ##* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=10|passage=Day and night, / Seedtime and harvest, heat and hoary frost, / Shall hold their '''course'''.|year=1873}} ## A [[programme]], a chosen manner of proceeding. ##: {{ux|en|Doubts arose about the expediency of such a '''course''' in the present crisis.}} ## Any ordered process or sequence of steps. ## {{lb|en|education}} A [[learning]] [[programme]] ### a series of [[lectures]] or [[lessons]] in a particular [[subject]] ###: {{syn|en|class}} ###: {{ux|en|I need to take a French '''course'''.}} ### {{lb|en|UK|Ireland|Philippines}} an [[educational]] programme at a [[college]] or [[university]] leading to an academic [[degree]] or vocational [[qualification]]. ###: {{ux|en|What's your '''course''' in university?
—Business studies. And you?}} ###* {{quote-book|en|year=1661|author={{w|John Fell (bishop)|John Fell}}|title=The Life of the most learned, reverend and pious Dr. H. Hammond|url=http://archive.org/stream/a615775104worduoft/a615775104worduoft_djvu.txt |passage=During the whole time of his abode in the university he generally spent thirteen hours of the day in study; by which assiduity besides an exact dispatch of the whole '''course''' of philosophy, he read over in a manner all classic authors that are extant{{...}}}} ##* {{quote-journal|en|date=August 21 1992|author=w:Edwina Currie|journal=Diary |passage=Her '''course''' will be ‘[[communication studies|Communication Studies]] with Theatre Studies’: [[God]], how tedious, how pointless.}} ##* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-07-20|volume=408|issue=8845| title=[http://www.economist.com/news/http://www.economist.com/news/business/21582001-army-new-online-courses-scaring-wits-out-traditional-universities-can-they The attack of the MOOCs]| passage=Since the launch early last year of […] two Silicon Valley start-ups offering free education through MOOCs, massive open online '''courses''', the ivory towers of academia have been shaken to their foundations. University brands built in some cases over centuries have been forced to contemplate the possibility that information technology will rapidly make their existing business model obsolete.}} ## {{lb|en|especially in|_|medicine}} A treatment plan. ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1932|author=w:Agatha Christie|title=w:The Thirteen Problems |passage=Miss Clark, alarmed at her increasing stoutness, was doing a '''course''' of what is popularly known as banting.}} ## {{lb|en|culinary}} A stage of a meal. ##: {{ux|en|We offer seafood as the first '''course'''.}} ## The succession of one to another in office or duty; order; turn. ##* {{RQ:KJV|2 Chronicles|8|14|passage=He appointed {{...}} the '''courses''' of the priests.}} # A path that something or someone moves along. #: {{ux|en|His illness ran its '''course'''.}} ## The itinerary of a race. ##: {{ux|en|The cross-country '''course''' passes the canal.}} ## A [[racecourse]]. ## The path taken by a flow of water; a [[watercourse]]. ## {{lb|en|sports}} The [[trajectory]] of a ball, frisbee etc. ## {{lb|en|golf}} A [[golf course]]. ## {{lb|en|nautical}} The direction of movement of a vessel at any given moment. ##: {{ux|en|The ship changed its '''course''' 15 degrees towards south.}} ## {{lb|en|navigation}} The intended passage of voyage, such as a boat, ship, airplane, spaceship, etc. ##: {{ux|en|A '''course''' was plotted to traverse the ocean.}} ##: {{ux|en|The pilot headed the plane on a northeasterly '''course'''.}} ## {{lb|en|India|historical}} The [[drive]] usually frequented by [[European]]s at an [[Indian]] [[station]]. # {{lb|en|nautical}} The lowest square sail in a fully rigged mast, often named according to the mast. #: {{ux|en|Main '''course''' and mainsail are the same thing in a sailing ship.}} # {{lb|en|in the plural|'''[[courses]]'''|obsolete|euphemistic}} [[menses#English|Menses]]. # A row or file of objects. ## {{senseid|en|masonry}}{{lb|en|masonry}} A row of bricks or blocks. ##: {{ux|en|On a building that size, two crews could only lay two '''courses''' in a day.}} ## {{lb|en|roofing}} A row of material that forms the [[roofing]], waterproofing or flashing system. ## {{lb|en|textiles}} In [[weft]] [[knitting]], a single row of [[loop]]s connecting the loops of the preceding and following rows. # {{lb|en|music}} One or more strings on some musical instruments (such as the [[guitar]], [[lute]] or [[vihuela]]): if multiple, then closely spaced, tuned in unison or octaves and intended to be played together. =====Hyponyms===== * {{l|en|bird course}} * {{l|en|crash
